files.purpose: Defines the chat box at the bottom of a chat column: ComposerArea stacks pending ApprovalCards over a tab slot (follow-up queue tab or changes tab) and the ComposerView pill, which holds the growing text column (quote/command chips, attachment strip, a 5-second attachment-limit notice, the AppKit-backed ComposerTextView) and, only when the runtime's thread resolves (`if let thread { ComposerControls(...) }`, lines 160-174), the trailing controls (paperclip with optional Recent Downloads popover, model/effort chip, context/usage ring, send/stop button). It also owns the composer's keyboard semantics (Return send or interrupt-and-send, Command-Return steer/queue as a fallback path only (the doc comment at lines 384-387 says the menu owns the chord while a turn runs, so steer() sees it only when that command is disabled or rebound), up/down prompt history recall, Escape stop/take-back or panel close, delete-at-start removing a chip), the @-file and /-command suggestion engine rendered in a caret-anchored popover, and the FileIndex that lists (git ls-files or a filtered directory walk) and scores workspace paths off the main actor.

Word boundaries for @ and / detection are only 0x20, 0x0A and 0x09 (lines 446-449); 0x0D (CR), U+2028 and U+2029 are not boundaries. With CRLF line breaks the character directly before a word typed on a new line is still 0x0A, so detection works; a text store that ends lines with a lone CR or a Unicode line/paragraph separator would make the word run back across the break and defeat @ and / detection. The Windows text control must store line breaks as LF or CRLF for identical behaviour.

Path handling assumes '/' separators: Entry.name = `(lowercased as NSString).lastPathComponent` (line 1168), the suggestion title `(path as NSString).lastPathComponent` (line 461) and `ToolTitles.relativePath(url.path, to: directory)` (line 1283); git ls-files output uses '/'. A Windows directory walk yielding '\' separators would change the name-based scores (1000/800/600) and the titles unless paths are normalised to '/'.

The enumerate() skip list is an exact, case-sensitive match on url.lastPathComponent (line 1278); on a case-insensitive file system such as NTFS a folder named, for example, "Node_Modules" or "Build" would not be skipped by this test.

feature_notes: Diff popover coordination: onAppear and on threadID change call diffPopover.sync(isVisible: runtime.isDiffVisible); isDiffVisible changes sync; diffOpenRequest change calls reopen; onDisappear and column hidden close it. The changes-tab action clears diff focus, sets diffAnchor nil, clears diffSelection if set, and sets isDiffVisible true only when it was false (written last).

Suggestion list lifecycle: onChange(suggestions) shows AnyView(suggestionMenu()) with itemCount or hides; hidden on disappear, on thread change and when the column is hidden; column shown again refocuses only if takesFocusOnAppear. Command list changes re-run cursorMoved if focused; commandErrors change re-shows the list if focused and visible.
blur(): if the click was not inside the suggestion popover, cancels controller.suggestionRefresh and clears suggestions.

handleKey with the list visible: up = max(0, selected - 1); down = min(count - 1, selected + 1); tab/submit/steer pick the selected item; escape sets dismissedSuggestions and clears; deleteAtStart returns false (not consumed). Without the list: submit -> send(); steer -> steer(); up/down -> recall; escape -> takeBackRunningTurn if running, else hide terminal if visible, else toggleDiff if diff visible, else not consumed; tab not consumed; deleteAtStart removes draft.command first, else the last quote (both animated with Chrome.panelSlide), else not consumed.
send(): no-op on empty draft; clears historyIndex and suggestions; running -> runtime.interruptAndSend() (comment: with heads at work it queues instead), idle -> runtime.send().

steer(): no-op on empty draft; clears historyIndex and suggestions; queues via runtime.queueDraftAsFollowUp() only when runtime.canQueue and the queueChat chord equals keyCode 36 + command; otherwise runtime.send(). The else branch applies in the running state too: when the queueChat chord is rebound away from KeyChord(keyCode: 36, modifiers: .command) or !runtime.canQueue, steer() calls runtime.send() even while a turn runs, unlike send(), which calls runtime.interruptAndSend() while running (lines 374-378). Doc comment verbatim (lines 384-387): "Command-Return: steer the running turn by queueing the draft behind it. Idle, there is nothing to steer behind, so it just sends. The menu owns the chord while a turn runs; this path only sees it when the command is disabled or rebound, so it falls back to send once the chord moves." So steer() is a fallback: while a turn runs, Command-Return is normally handled by the menu command, not by the text view.

recall(older:): prompts = sentPrompts without empty strings; not consumed if none or if the draft has attachments; allowed only when the text is empty or equals the prompt at historyIndex. Older: next = (recalledIndex ?? count) - 1, returns true without change at the oldest. Newer: requires a recalled index; moves forward or, past the newest, clears historyIndex and text.

cursorMoved: resets dismissedSuggestions, calls runtime.warmSession() if the text is non-empty, cancels the previous refresh Task and starts a new @MainActor Task whose body is `guard !dismissedSuggestions else { return }; await refreshSuggestions(cursor: controller.cursorLocation)` (lines 433-436), so an Escape that sets dismissedSuggestions after the Task was scheduled suppresses that refresh.

refreshSuggestions: first `guard cursor > 0, cursor <= text.length else { if suggestions.isVisible { suggestions = SuggestionState() }; return }` (lines 441-444), so a caret at position 0 or past the end hides the list. Then word = run of characters before the caret back to space (0x20), newline (0x0A) or tab (0x09), in UTF-16 units. '@' prefix: fileIndex.search(rest), drops result if cancelled, items value "@<path> " title lastPathComponent detail path symbol "doc". '/' prefix only when the word starts at index 0: kind .command. Empty items hide the list. Selection is kept (clamped) only if the range location is unchanged, else 0.

commandSuggestions: built-ins first "plan" detail "Turn plan mode on or off"; "compact" detail "Summarize the conversation to free up context" when provider.supportsCompact (Provider.swift:151 at B2: .codex, .claude, .copilot, .deepseek, .meta, .zai, .pi); then provider commands for commandKey; ranked by SlashCommand.suggestions with recentCommands[provider.rawValue]; value "/<name> ", title "/<name>", symbol "command" for built-in else "sparkles".

pick(): command kind with a SlashCommand removes the typed word and sets runtime.draft.command = DraftCommand(...) animated, then focuses; otherwise replaces the word with suggestion.value (file mention with trailing space) and focuses.

attach(): room = max(0, 8 - current count); dropped = sources.count - min(sources.count, room); Storage.attach does the actual adding. Notice strings verbatim: single image source "The image was left out: a message holds 8 attachments"; one dropped "One file was left out: a message holds 8 attachments"; else "<n> files were left out: a message holds 8 attachments" (8 is Self.maxAttachments interpolated). Always refocuses. Notice clears after Task.sleep 5 s with Chrome.panelSlide via `.task(id: attachmentNotice) { guard attachmentNotice != nil else { return }; try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(5)); guard !Task.isCancelled else { return }; withAnimation(Chrome.panelSlide) { attachmentNotice = nil } }` (lines 219-225). The wait restarts only when the notice string changes: note() only assigns `attachmentNotice = message` (line 523), so two consecutive drops that produce the same message (for example both "One file was left out: a message holds 8 attachments") leave the task id unchanged, the timer does not restart, and the notice clears 5 s after the first drop. The source comment "a second drop restarts the wait" holds only for a different message.

chooseFiles(): NSOpenPanel allowsMultipleSelection true, canChooseDirectories false, prompt "Attach"; on .OK attaches panel.urls as .file sources. Paperclip opens DownloadsPopover when settings.recentDownloadsPicker is true, else chooseFiles directly; popover pick closes it then attaches the URL; chooseOther closes it then runs chooseFiles.

goesToHead = hydraAlwaysHeads && hydraIsOn; queueGoesToHead = (hydraQueueHeads || hydraAlwaysHeads) && hydraIsOn; headsProvider = hydraHeadsProvider(of: pair) when hydra is on and a pair exists, nil when equal to the thread's provider.

ContextMeter hasCredits = CreditsReader.exposesCredits(provider) && settings.hasAPIKey(for: provider). Ring hidden entirely while the usage panel is popped out (settings.showsUsagePanel). Pop-out closes the popover then sets showsUsagePanel = true with Chrome.panelSlide.
SendDraftState action: running -> runtime.interrupt() (not interruptAndSend), idle -> send closure. SendShortcutText caches ShortcutStore label/hint once per process.

DraftAttachments: delete button removes by id without animation block; onChange(attachments) retires preview entries not in the set; onDisappear closes the preview. Arrival animation only for ids not yet in drawn.

FileIndex.prepare: sets directory; loops while not cancelled and directory unchanged: if a cache entry exists, assigns its entries and returns unless `Date.now.timeIntervalSince(cached.builtAt) > Self.freshness` (strictly greater than 60 s, so an age of exactly 60 s is still fresh); a stale cache is kept in `entries` and served while the rebuild runs behind it (line 1122 comment: "A stale index is served and rebuilt behind it."); `entries = []` happens only when there is no cache at all; joins an in-flight build for the same directory; if `Self.building.count >= 2`, awaits `Self.building.values.first` (an arbitrary element of an unordered Dictionary, not necessarily the oldest build) and then `continue`s, re-reading the cache; else starts a build Task that inserts into the cache and removes itself from building. Applies fresh entries only if still current and not cancelled.
FileIndex.build: Entry lowercased path, name = lastPathComponent of the lowercased path, lengthPenalty = min(path.count, 99), isASCII = all UTF-8 bytes < 128.

FileIndex.search: empty needle returns the first limit (8) paths in index order. Scoring: name == needle 1000; name prefix 800; substring of name 600; substring of full lowercased path 400; subsequence of lowercased path 100; minus lengthPenalty. Keeps a top-limit list by insertion (ties keep earlier entries first since insertion is before the first strictly lower score); checks cancellation every 2,048 entries and returns [] when cancelled.

contains(): ASCII fast path with memmem on UTF-8 bytes; falls back to String.contains if the haystack contains byte 13 (carriage return) or storage is not contiguous. isSubsequence(): ASCII byte walk, restarting in grapheme mode on byte 13; non-ASCII uses Character comparison.

FileIndex.list: if Git(directory).isRepository() and listFiles() non-empty, first 60,000 files; else enumerate(): skips hidden files and package descendants, skips names node_modules, build, dist, .build, DerivedData, Pods, target, and any item deeper than level 16 (skipDescendants). The test is `skipped.contains(url.lastPathComponent) || enumerator.level > 16` (line 1278), an exact case-sensitive Set match on the last path component applied before the isDirectory check, so it also skips plain files with those names, not only directories; an item at level > 16 is itself skipped, not just its descendants. It then excludes directories, stores ToolTitles.relativePath(url.path, to: directory), stops at 20,000 results.

files.purpose: Implements the paperclip button's Recent Downloads popover, shown when the recentDownloadsPicker setting is on. RecentDownloads scans the user's Downloads folder off the main actor for the 15 most recently modified non-hidden files, formats their sizes and loads 30-point square thumbnails for image files, and DownloadsPopover renders them as 38-point rows in a 360-point-wide popover with Show in Finder and Choose Files exits; picking a row calls AttachmentDrops.shared.arm(image:fromScreen:radius: 6) with the row's preview image and its screen frame (what AttachmentDrops then animates, and toward what, is defined elsewhere), dismisses the popover and then calls pick(url).
key_symbols: struct RecentDownload: Identifiable, Hashable { var url: URL; var name: String; var size: String?; var isImage: Bool; var id: String { url.path } }

@MainActor @Observable final class RecentDownloads { nonisolated static let limit = 15; nonisolated static let previewPointSize: CGFloat = 30; private(set) var items: [RecentDownload] = []; private(set) var thumbnails: [String: CGImage] = [:]; private(set) var isLoaded = false; var directory: URL?; private nonisolated static let imageExtensions: Set<String>; private static let sizeFormatter: ByteCountFormatter; func load() async }

struct DownloadsPopover: View { let pick: (URL) -> Void; let chooseOther: () -> Void; @State private var downloads = RecentDownloads(); private var height: CGFloat?; private static func height(forRows count: Int) -> CGFloat }

private struct DownloadRow: View { static let height: CGFloat = 38; let item: RecentDownload; let thumbnail: CGImage?; let pick: () -> Void; @State isHovering = false; @State previewFrame: CGRect = .zero; @Environment(keypath dismiss) dismiss; @ViewBuilder private var preview: some View }

feature_notes: load(): returns if no Downloads directory. Detached scan lists the folder with keys contentModificationDate, fileSize, isDirectory, isHidden and option skipsHiddenFiles (a failed listing yields []); drops entries whose resource values fail or which are directories (isDirectory must be exactly false, so nil also drops); sorts by modification date descending with `.sorted { $0.1 > $1.1 }` (line 56) and no tie-break, so files with equal dates (including several with the .distantPast fallback for a missing date) have no order defined by this source (missing date = distantPast, missing size = 0); isHidden is fetched but never read; keeps the first 15.
Scan cancellation: withTaskCancellationHandler cancels the detached scan; the compactMap also checks Task.isCancelled per URL. After the scan, returns without publishing if cancelled.
Image detection: lowercased path extension in {png, jpg, jpeg, heic, heif, gif, tiff, tif, bmp, webp}.
Size string: ByteCountFormatter(.file).string(fromByteCount:) only when size > 0, else nil (no size label shown).

Publishing order: items, thumbnails reset to [:] and isLoaded = true are set inside the TaskGroup before awaiting thumbnails, so rows appear immediately with file icons and thumbnails fill in as each resolves (skipped if cancelled or nil).
Row pick order: arm the drop animation, dismiss(), then Task @MainActor pick() so the pick runs after the popover closes (comment: matching PopoverItem behavior).
Show in Finder opens the folder only when directory is non-nil; Choose Files… calls chooseOther.
